package: @astryxdesign/cli

# Quick Start

Create a new integration package or add Astryx to one you already publish.

## Quick start

### Make the package

An integration starts as a normal npm package. Make a folder for it, create a package.json inside that folder, give the package a name, make it an ES module, then install the Astryx CLI, Core, and TypeScript for development.

```bash
mkdir acme-widgets && cd acme-widgets
npm init -y  # only with npm: writes package.json
npm pkg set name=@acme/astryx-widgets type=module  # only with npm: edits package.json
npm pkg set 'exports={}' --json  # only with npm: edits package.json
npm install -D @astryxdesign/cli @astryxdesign/core typescript@6
```

- Set `"type": "module"`: the `.js` files the CLI generates, such as a built theme, are ES modules, and Node fails to load them in a package marked `"type": "commonjs"`, which `npm init -y` (only with npm: writes package.json) writes on npm 11.
- Start with `"exports": {}`: each component and template you add then writes the public import that `integration verify` resolves.
- Run the CLI as `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12`, which runs the `@astryxdesign/cli` you installed as a devDependency.
- Component commands read Core, so they need `@astryxdesign/core` installed.
- The checks compare your docs with your code through TypeScript's JavaScript compiler API, which `typescript` 5.0 through 6 has. TypeScript 7 does not ship that API: on TypeScript 7, also install `@typescript/typescript6`, its TypeScript 6 API package, and the checks use it.

### Add your first integration item

An integration can ship several kinds of items. Start with a component named `AcmeCarousel`.

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 integration add component AcmeCarousel
```

```text
component contribution added

[ok] AcmeCarousel

Declare component root ./components in astryx.integration.mjs.

- components/AcmeCarousel.doc.mjs
- components/AcmeCarousel.tsx
- package.json
- astryx.integration.mjs
```

`integration add` creates the component source, its `.doc.mjs`, the package export, and `astryx.integration.mjs`. Update the generated doc so the CLI understands the component, then write the component itself.

Read it back the way an app will.

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 component AcmeCarousel
```

You now have an integration package with one exported component.

### Check it in every build (required)

Run `integration check --strict` in every build (`npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/ship/checks`): a doc, prop, template, or link that drifts from the code then fails your build, not your users' apps. Set it up now, as the `typecheck` script, and run it.

```bash
npm pkg set scripts.typecheck="astryx integration check --strict"  # only with npm: edits package.json
npm run typecheck
```

```text
[ok] 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 skipped. Every check passed.
```

- Run `typecheck` in CI and before every publish. When you add a `tsconfig.json`, put `tsc --noEmit && ` in front of the check so the same script checks your types.
- What each check covers, and what `--strict` adds: `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/ship/checks`.

### Verify and pack the package

Run `integration verify` to check that an app would see the component, then make the `.tgz` file you install next. `--pack-destination ..` writes it beside the package folder, so the next pack does not ship it.

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 integration verify
npm pack --pack-destination ..  # only with npm: builds the publish tarball
```

```text
Integration package ready

[ok] @acme/astryx-widgets@1.0.0

4 packed files; 3/3 required files present.
```

`integration verify` installs the packed package in a temporary app and confirms the component resolves through its public import there (`npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/ship/checks`). It publishes nothing and leaves no `.tgz` file, so `npm pack` (only with npm: builds the publish tarball) writes `../acme-astryx-widgets-1.0.0.tgz` for the next step.

### Use it in an app

Install Core, the CLI, and your `.tgz` file in a new app. The app loads your package because it is a dependency, with no config.

```bash
cd ..
mkdir my-app && cd my-app
npm init -y  # only with npm: writes package.json
npm install @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/cli ../acme-astryx-widgets-1.0.0.tgz
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 component AcmeCarousel
```

```text
**Import:** `import {AcmeCarousel} from '@acme/astryx-widgets/components/AcmeCarousel';`
```

The next sections explain each package field and the integration file. To build the real component, continue with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/building-blocks/components`.

## Fill in package.json

An integration is an ordinary npm package. These six fields control how it is named, developed, checked, and published.

`peerDependencies` are packages the app supplies. `devDependencies` are packages you use while building the integration.

Field              | Set it to                                                                                                                                                                                     | Why                                                                                                                
------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`name`             | Your package name, such as `@acme/astryx-widgets`                                                                                                                                             | Each add writes it into the `import` of the doc it generates. Rename before you add, or update each `import` after.
`version`          | The release you publish, such as `1.0.0`                                                                                                                                                      | Apps see it; `astryx.integration.mjs` never repeats it.                                                            
`exports`          | Start with `{}`                                                                                                                                                                               | Each component and template add writes its public import here, and `integration verify` resolves it.               
`files`            | Optional: the paths to publish                                                                                                                                                                | Keeps private files out. When the list exists, each add appends its root and `astryx.integration.mjs`.             
`peerDependencies` | `@astryxdesign/core` when your code imports it; `@astryxdesign/cli`, optional, when you ship a feature that needs a newer CLI (`npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/ship/versioning`) | The app supplies these packages for your integration.                                                              
`devDependencies`  | `@astryxdesign/cli`, `@astryxdesign/core`, and `typescript`                                                                                                                                   | Lets you run the CLI, build components, and run the checks while working on the integration.                       

Peer ranges and releases are covered in `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/ship/versioning`; `files` and publishing in `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/ship/publishing`. Add `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit && astryx integration check --strict"` to `scripts` so each run checks your types and that your docs, props, and links still match the code. It needs `typescript` and a `tsconfig.json`; see `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/ship/checks`.

## The integration file

The first `integration add` creates `astryx.integration.mjs`, and each later add updates it. You do not need to write or edit this file during the quick start.

### Files in the package

- `package.json` defines the npm package, including its name, version, dependencies, published files, and exports.
- `astryx.integration.mjs` tells the CLI where the package keeps each kind of integration item.
- The integration item files live under those roots. For example, a component can have `AcmeWidget.tsx` for its source and `AcmeWidget.doc.mjs` for its documentation.

### Fields in the integration file

astryx.integration.mjs:
```javascript
/** @type {import('@astryxdesign/cli/authoring').AstryxIntegration} */
export default {
  components: './components',
};
```

The file tells the CLI where this package keeps its integration items. Edit it only when you want a custom root or another optional setting. Paths are relative to package.json, and later adds keep a custom path you already set.

Every field is in `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring integration`.

### Use the CLI

You can edit the package files by hand, but the CLI handles the normal workflow. These links always open the canonical command docs.

astryx integration add: Add one working contribution to an integration package. Read it with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/integration-add`.

astryx integration verify: Check the package the way npm will publish it, before you publish. Read it with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/integration-verify`.

astryx doctor integration: Check an integration package while authoring it. Read it with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/doctor-integration`.

## In global mode

In global mode: users can also install your package for their computer, beside the global CLI (`npm install -g @astryxdesign/cli your-package`). It then applies in folders outside any project, and inside a project only if the project installs it. See `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global` and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/global-integrations`.
